name: Joseph Moran
life: “I still remember selling my first strip of land to a family with a van.” Friday often includes a stop at Studio Boulevard, where Joseph waits by the window where the whole crossing can be seen without leaning into the road.
voice: I made money selling buildings. I thought the finest gift I could give her was never having to ask a landlord for anything.
appearance: Joseph is easy to recognize by gray hair trimmed very close behind the ears and a straight nose and deep-set eyes. Usually dressed in a boxy denim jacket with a thin silver ring worn on a cord, Joseph raises one eyebrow long before saying yes when listening.
personality: Joseph has excellent recall for voices and a poor memory for official titles. Someone who waited patiently at a counter years ago is more likely to be remembered than the person in charge.
agenda: To offer the daughter security on terms she can decline.
family: Jo Bloom is Joseph’s younger cousin. Joseph is allowed to ask about the bad news afterward. Jo calls about good news first. Neither wants every family conversation to begin with a bill, a diagnosis or an apology. Asked about *The soft wharf chalk*, Jo says, “I thought it was a safety warning and stopped a delivery.”
connections: Cassandra Collins (daughter). A wealthy father and a young tailor disagree about whether owning a whole building constitutes freedom.

reactions.situation: The daughter declines the property gift
reactions.response: Joseph takes the daughter's preferred shop seriously before proposing another gift.
